text: When you build a REST API, good design makes it easy for other developers to use. Start by giving your endpoints clear, simple names that describe the resources they represent. Use the correct HTTP status codes so clients know what happened—for example, 200 for success or 404 when something is not found. Always provide clear documentation that explains each endpoint and its parameters. Finally, plan for change by using versioning, such as /v1/ or /v2/ in the URL. Following these practices keeps your API consistent, reliable, and simple for everyone who works with it.
